name: Tony Rominger
milestone_by_age_26: Turned professional in 1986 at age 25 and won multiple professional races including GP Jurassia and GP Lausanne.
early_history_summary: Born in Vejle, Denmark but grew up in Menzingen, Switzerland. Began cycling relatively late, spurred by competition with his younger brother Lars. Rode for amateur teams Allegro-Puch in 1984-85 before turning professional with Cilo-Aufina-Gemeaz in 1986, winning several races that year.
family_context_summary: Born in Vejle, Denmark; grew up in Menzingen in the canton of Zug, Switzerland. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: late specialization, sibling competition, European cycling ecosystem
evidence_summary: Rominger began cycling late, motivated by competition with his younger brother, and turned professional at 25 in 1986, winning several races that year. His family background is not documented in reviewed sources. He benefited from the strong European cycling ecosystem but showed no particular early advantage beyond natural physical talent for climbing and time-trialling.
starting_point: Born in Vejle, Denmark to a family that later settled in Menzingen, Switzerland; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from professional cycling in 1997; lives in Monaco; later married Swiss singer Francine Jordi.

trajectory.event: Turned professional with Cilo-Aufina-Gemeaz and won multiple races including GP Jurassia and GP Lausanne.
Won Tirreno-Adriatico and Giro di Lombardia, establishing himself as a top stage racer.
Won the first of three consecutive Vuelta a Espana titles.
Won all three jerseys at the Vuelta a Espana and placed second at the Tour de France.
Broke the world hour record twice and won the UCI Road World Cup.
Won the Giro d'Italia, his fourth Grand Tour victory.
Retired from professional cycling.

name: Yingluck Shinawatra
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26, had a master's degree and was working as a mid-level manager at a family company; no independent material milestone found.
early_history_summary: Born into a wealthy Thai family of Chinese descent; father was an MP and brother Thaksin became prime minister. Earned a master's in public administration from Kentucky State University in 1991, then returned to work at family firms.
family_context_summary: Youngest of nine children born into a wealthy family of Chinese descent that settled in the Chiang Mai area. Father was a member of parliament; brother Thaksin Shinawatra became prime minister.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family was deeply involved in business and politics; brother Thaksin founded a telecoms empire and became prime minister. Father was an MP from the late 1960s to mid-1970s.
evidence_summary: Yingluck Shinawatra was born into a wealthy and politically connected Thai family. By age 26, she held a master's degree and was working as a Production Director at the family firm Shinawatra Directories. Her career advancement was entirely within family businesses, with no independent material milestone by age 26. Her real success as president of AIS and later prime minister came well after 26.

name: Fred Anton Maier
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic bronze (5,000m) and silver (10,000m) at the 1964 Innsbruck Winter Olympics at age 25.
early_history_summary: Born on the island of Nøtterøy, Norway, to a farmer father. Combined farming with speed skating and cycling from a young age. Won bronze at the Norwegian national time trial cycling championship at 18 in 1957, and Norwegian all-around speed skating bronze in 1961 at age 22. Was named to the national team for the 1964 Olympics.
family_context_summary: Born on Nøtterøy, Norway; father Anton Maier was a hunter and later farmer. Maier combined farming with his athletic career throughout his life.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a farmer and hunter; no documented connection to speed skating or cycling.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Norwegian skating ecosystem, dual-sport talent, farming livelihood, long-distance specialization
evidence_summary: Maier grew up on the island of Nøtterøy in Norway, the heartland of speed skating, and combined farming with athletics from a young age. He won a cycling bronze at the Norwegian national championship at 18 and earned Norwegian all-around speed skating bronze at 22. By 25, he won two Olympic medals at Innsbruck 1964. His father was a farmer, providing a stable rural livelihood that accommodated training.
starting_point: Born on the island of Nøtterøy, Norway; father Anton Maier was a hunter and later farmer, providing a rural working-class upbringing.
current_position: Died on June 9, 2015 at age 76 in Nøtterøy, Norway; final role: farmer and retired Olympic champion speed skater.

trajectory.event: Won bronze medal at Norwegian national time trial cycling championship.
Won Norwegian all-around speed skating bronze medal.
Won Olympic bronze (5,000m) and silver (10,000m) at Innsbruck Winter Olympics.
Won Norwegian all-around speed skating championship and set first world record.
Awarded Egebergs Ærespris for achievements in both speed skating and cycling.
Won Olympic gold (5,000m), World Allround Championship, European Championship, and Oscar Mathisen Award.
Died on June 9, 2015, in Nøtterøy, Norway.

name: Colin Renfrew
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26, was a research student at Cambridge; PhD, first academic appointment, and influential publications all came after age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Stockton-on-Tees, raised in Welwyn Garden City, educated at St Albans School. Interested in archaeology from a young age, excavating in Canterbury as a teenager. Did National Service in the RAF (1956-58), then studied at St John's College, Cambridge, graduating in 1962. Elected president of the Cambridge Union in 1961.
family_context_summary: Born in Stockton-on-Tees, raised in Welwyn Garden City; educated at St Albans School. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Renfrew was interested in archaeology from a young age and excavated as a teenager, but his material archaeological milestones all came after age 26. He graduated from Cambridge at 25, was president of the Cambridge Union at 24, but completed his PhD at 28, got his first academic appointment at 28, and published his first influential paper at 31. The Cambridge Union presidency was a debating achievement, not an archaeological milestone.

name: Artūrs Irbe
milestone_by_age_26: Won World Championship gold with the Soviet Union in 1989 and 1990, was named best goalkeeper of the 1990 tournament, and helped Dinamo Riga reach the Soviet Hockey League finals in 1988.
early_history_summary: Born in Riga, Latvia (then Soviet Union). Started playing hockey at age 9 at the hockey school 'Latvijas bērzs.' Initially trained as a defenseman before switching to goaltender. Played for Latvian SSR championship teams before joining Dinamo Riga in the Soviet Hockey League at age 19-20, becoming starting goaltender in 1987-88.
family_context_summary: Born in Riga, Latvian SSR, Soviet Union. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet hockey pipeline, Dinamo Riga, early goaltender training, national team
evidence_summary: Irbe started hockey at age 9 in Riga and progressed through the Soviet hockey pipeline, joining Dinamo Riga at 19-20. He became the starting goaltender in 1987-88 and helped Dinamo Riga reach the Soviet League finals. He won World Championship gold with the Soviet Union in 1989 and 1990, being named best goalkeeper in 1990. His family background is not documented, but the Soviet sports system provided elite training infrastructure from a young age.
starting_point: Born in Riga, Latvian SSR, Soviet Union; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from professional hockey in 2007; served as goaltending coach for various NHL and international teams; inducted into IIHF Hall of Fame in 2010.

trajectory.event: Debuted for Dinamo Riga in the Soviet Hockey League.
Became Dinamo Riga's starting goaltender and helped the team reach the Soviet Hockey League finals.
Won World Championship gold with the Soviet Union national team.
Won second World Championship gold and was named best goalkeeper of the tournament.
Moved to North America and made NHL debut with the San Jose Sharks.
Selected to NHL All-Star Game and finished 5th in Vezina Trophy voting with a breakout season for San Jose.
Reached Stanley Cup Finals with the Carolina Hurricanes.
Inducted into the IIHF Hall of Fame.

name: Nam June Paik
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26, was a graduate student in Munich; first major exhibition 'Exposition of Music/Electronic Television' came in 1963 at age 30.
early_history_summary: Born in Seoul to a wealthy textile manufacturing family. Trained as a classical pianist in Seoul, fled to Japan during the Korean War. Graduated from University of Tokyo in 1956 with a thesis on Schoenberg. Moved to West Germany in 1957 to study music history at Munich University, where he met John Cage in 1958.
family_context_summary: Born in Seoul to a wealthy family of textile manufacturers. Family fled to Japan during the Korean War.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family was wealthy in textile manufacturing; no documented connection to art or music beyond Paik's own training as a classical pianist.
evidence_summary: Paik was born into a wealthy Korean textile family and trained as a classical pianist, graduating from the University of Tokyo at 24. He moved to Germany to study music and met John Cage at 26, which was influential but not a material milestone. His first major exhibition, which is considered the starting point of video art, came in 1963 at age 30. No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Simon Cowell
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Fanfare Records at 25-26 but first documented hit 'So Macho' by Sinitta came in 1986 at age 27; no material milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in London to a well-to-do family; father was an EMI music industry executive and mother a former ballet dancer. Dropped out of school at 16 and landed a mailroom job at EMI through his father. Became A&R assistant at EMI in 1979, then co-founded E&S Music in the early 1980s before leaving in 1983. Co-founded Fanfare Records in 1985.
family_context_summary: Born in London to a well-to-do British household; father Eric Philip Cowell was an EMI music industry executive, mother Julie Brett was a former ballet dancer and socialite. Raised with nannies and attended several boarding schools.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a music industry executive at EMI who secured Cowell his first job in the EMI mailroom. Direct parental industry connection was the primary career catalyst.
evidence_summary: Cowell was born into a well-to-do family with his father as an EMI executive, which secured him a mailroom job at EMI at 16. He worked his way up to A&R assistant by 20, co-founded E&S Music in the early 1980s (which reportedly had several hits, though specifics are undocumented), and co-founded Fanfare Records in 1985 at age 25-26. However, his first clearly documented hit song, 'So Macho' by Sinitta, came in 1986 at age 27. No specific, dated, material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Andy Hug
milestone_by_age_26: Won the European Kyokushin Championships in 1985 at age 21 and again in 1989, and became the first non-Japanese fighter to reach the final of the Kyokushin World Open in 1987.
early_history_summary: Born in Wohlen, Switzerland; given up for adoption and raised by grandparents after time in an orphanage. Started Kyokushin karate at age 10 under Werner Schenker. Won the Swiss Oyama Cup at 15 with special age exemption, joined the Swiss national team at 17, and won the Swiss Championships at 18. Competed in his first Kyokushin World Open in 1984 at age 20.
family_context_summary: Born in Wohlen, Switzerland; father died before seeing him, mother unable to care for him, placed in orphanage then raised by grandparents from age 3.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family connection to martial arts; grandparents initially opposed karate training but grandmother eventually convinced grandfather to relent.
primary_early_advantage_tags: orphaned upbringing, early karate start, prodigy talent, bullying catalyst, Swiss national team
evidence_summary: Hug was given up for adoption and raised by his grandparents in Wohlen, Switzerland. He started Kyokushin karate at 10 to defend against bullying and showed exceptional talent, winning the Swiss Oyama Cup at 15 with a special age exemption. By 21, he won the European Championships and later became the first non-Japanese World Open finalist at 23. His early adversity—orphaned, bullied, financially constrained—catalyzed his intense dedication to karate.
starting_point: Born in Wohlen, Switzerland; father died before meeting him, mother unable to cope, placed in orphanage then raised by grandparents from age 3.
current_position: Died on August 24, 2000 at age 35 in Tokyo from acute promyelocytic leukemia; final role: K-1 Grand Prix champion and martial arts superstar in Japan.

trajectory.event: Won the Swiss Oyama Cup national Kyokushin competition with a special age exemption.
Won the European Kyokushin Championships for the first time.
Became the first non-Japanese fighter to reach the final of the Kyokushin World Open.
Won his second European Kyokushin Championships title.
Won the Seidokaikan Karate World Cup, transitioning to professional fighting.
Won the K-1 Grand Prix tournament, becoming the best martial arts fighter in the world.
Died of acute promyelocytic leukemia on August 24 in Tokyo.

name: Andrzej Żuławski
milestone_by_age_26: Made his directorial debut in 1967 at age 26 with two short television films, 'The Song of Triumphant Love' and 'Pavoncello,' both of which won accolades in Los Angeles.
early_history_summary: Born in Lviv, Ukraine (then Poland). Moved with his father to Czechoslovakia and later Poland. Studied cinema at IDHEC in Paris, graduating in 1965, and philosophy at the Sorbonne. Worked as assistant to Andrzej Wajda on several films in the early 1960s and was a film critic for the weekly 'Film.'
family_context_summary: Born in Lviv to Mirosław Żuławski, a well-known writer, journalist, and diplomat. Great-uncle Jerzy Żuławski was a noted novelist. The family moved through Czechoslovakia and Poland.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Mirosław Żuławski was a writer and diplomat who co-wrote the script for Andrzej's first feature film. Great-uncle Jerzy Żuławski wrote the 'Moon Trilogy' that Andrzej later adapted for film.
primary_early_advantage_tags: literary family, IDHEC film school, Wajda mentorship, Polish-French cultural network
evidence_summary: Żuławski was born into a prominent Polish literary family—his father Mirosław was a writer and diplomat, and his great-uncle Jerzy was a novelist. He studied at IDHEC in Paris and worked as assistant to Andrzej Wajda, Poland's leading director. His directorial debut in 1967 with two short TV films that won accolades benefited from his father's literary connections (his first feature was based on his father's novel) and his elite film education.
starting_point: Born in Lviv to Mirosław Żuławski, a well-known writer, journalist, and diplomat; raised in a prominent Polish literary and diplomatic family.
current_position: Died on February 17, 2016 at age 75; final role: film director and writer known for art-house films including Possession (1981).

trajectory.event: Graduated from IDHEC film school in Paris after working as assistant to Andrzej Wajda.
Made directorial debut with two short television films that won accolades in Los Angeles.
Released first feature film 'The Third Part of the Night,' based on his father's novel.
Second feature 'The Devil' was banned by communist censors in Poland.
Achieved French breakthrough with 'That Most Important Thing: Love' starring Romy Schneider.
Released 'Possession,' his most famous film, nominated for the Palme d'Or at Cannes.
Died on February 17, 2016.

name: Conor McGregor
milestone_by_age_26: Became Cage Warriors double champion (featherweight and lightweight) in 2012 at age 24, then signed with the UFC and won his UFC debut in April 2013 at age 25.
early_history_summary: Born in Crumlin, Dublin, to working-class parents. Started boxing at age 11 at Crumlin Boxing Club, won Dublin Novice Championship at 16. Met Tom Egan and began MMA training around 2006. Started training at SBG Dublin under John Kavanagh in 2008. Made amateur MMA debut at 18 and professional debut at 19 in 2008, abandoning a plumbing apprenticeship to focus on fighting.
family_context_summary: Born to Tony and Margaret McGregor in Crumlin, Dublin, a working-class neighborhood. Father was a taxi driver; family had limited financial means. Parents opposed his decision to abandon plumbing for fighting.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family connection to combat sports; parents opposed his fighting career choice.
primary_early_advantage_tags: working-class background, boxing foundation, SBG Dublin, Kavanagh mentorship, MMA wave, self-belief
evidence_summary: McGregor grew up in working-class Crumlin, Dublin, and started boxing at 11, winning a Dublin Novice Championship at 16. He transitioned to MMA at 18, training at SBG Dublin under John Kavanagh. Despite financial hardship—including unemployment and relying on his girlfriend for transport—he abandoned a plumbing apprenticeship to focus fully on fighting. By 24, he was a double Cage Warriors champion, leading to a UFC contract at 25. His adversity and self-belief were central catalysts.
starting_point: Born in Crumlin, Dublin to working-class parents; father was a taxi driver, limited financial means.
current_position: Former UFC double champion and global MMA superstar; estimated net worth ~$200M; resides in Dublin. Has not fought since 2021 due to injury; scheduled to return vs Max Holloway in July 2026.

trajectory.event: Made professional MMA debut, winning by second-round TKO.
Became Cage Warriors double champion, winning both featherweight and lightweight titles.
Signed with UFC and won debut fight by first-round TKO.
Knocked out Jose Aldo in 13 seconds to become undisputed UFC Featherweight Champion.
Won UFC Lightweight Championship at UFC 205, becoming the first UFC double champion.
Fought Floyd Mayweather Jr. in a blockbuster boxing match, losing by TKO in round 10.
Suffered severe leg injury at UFC 264, leading to extended hiatus from competition.

name: Gloria Estefan
milestone_by_age_26: As lead singer of Miami Sound Machine, signed with Discos CBS International in 1980 at age 23 and released four Spanish-language albums between 1981 and 1983 with hit songs across Spanish-speaking countries.
early_history_summary: Born in Havana, Cuba; family fled to Miami in 1959-60 after the Cuban Revolution. Father was a bodyguard for Batista who was imprisoned after the Bay of Pigs invasion and later served in Vietnam, returning with multiple sclerosis. Estefan cared for her ailing father and younger sister while attending University of Miami. Joined the Miami Latin Boys in 1975 at age 18, which became Miami Sound Machine.
family_context_summary: Born in Havana, Cuba to Jose Fajardo (a bodyguard for Batista's family) and Gloria Garcia. Family fled to Miami after the Cuban Revolution. Father was imprisoned after the Bay of Pigs invasion and later served in Vietnam, returning with multiple sclerosis. Estefan cared for him and her younger sister.
parent_family_domain_summary: Paternal family had musical connections—famous bandleader and flautist Jose Fajardo was in the lineage, and a classical pianist. Mother had singing talent and was offered a Hollywood dubbing role as a child. However, no direct parental music industry mentorship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cuban exile, Miami Latin music scene, Emilio Estefan partnership, CBS International, adversity catalyst
evidence_summary: Estefan fled Cuba as a toddler and grew up in Miami, where her father's imprisonment and illness forced her into a caregiving role. She joined the Miami Latin Boys at 18, which became Miami Sound Machine under Emilio Estefan's leadership. By 23, they signed with CBS International and released four Spanish-language albums with international hits. Her Cuban heritage and Miami's position as the Latin music frontier, combined with her partnership with Emilio Estefan, were key advantages.
starting_point: Born in Havana, Cuba to a family connected to the Batista government; father was a motorcycle police officer and bodyguard; family fled to Miami as refugees after the Cuban Revolution.
current_position: Global Latin pop icon with multiple Grammy Awards, Kennedy Center Honors, and Presidential Medal of Freedom; estimated net worth ~$500M with husband Emilio Estefan; resides in Miami.

trajectory.event: Joined the Miami Latin Boys, which was renamed Miami Sound Machine.
Miami Sound Machine signed with Discos CBS International.
Released 'Conga,' which became her signature song and launched Latin crossover pop.
Released multi-platinum album 'Let It Loose' with five hit singles including first Hot 100 No. 1.
Launched solo career with album 'Cuts Both Ways.'
Survived a serious bus crash and made a successful comeback with album 'Into the Light.'
Received Kennedy Center Honors, the first Cuban-American to do so.

name: Tania Bruguera
milestone_by_age_26: Achieved critical success at the 5th Havana Biennial in 1994 at age 26, marking the beginning of her international career, and participated in the Whitechapel Gallery's 'New Art from Cuba' exhibition the same year.
early_history_summary: Born in Havana, Cuba to diplomat and politician Miguel Brugueras, who served in Castro's government. Lived in Paris, Lebanon, and Panama as a child due to father's postings. Parents divorced over political differences in 1979. Started studying art at the Escuela Elemental de Artes Plásticas in Havana at age 12, then studied at the Instituto Superior de Arte.
family_context_summary: Born in Havana to Miguel Brugueras, a diplomat and politician in Castro's government who served as ambassador to Lebanon and Panama, and was also founder of Cuba's state security agencies. Parents divorced over political differences in 1979.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a diplomat and government minister, not an artist. His political position gave Bruguera unique exposure to international settings (Paris, Lebanon, Panama) and later became the subject of her political art.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cuban art education, diplomat father, Havana Biennial, political adversity, international childhood
evidence_summary: Bruguera was born into a high-ranking Cuban political family—her father was a diplomat and founder of state security agencies. She lived in Paris, Lebanon, and Panama as a child before her parents divorced over political differences. She attended elite Cuban art schools from age 12, studying under Juan Francisco Elso Padilla. By 26, she achieved critical success at the 5th Havana Biennial, launching her international career. Her father's political role and the subsequent conflict with him became central to her political art practice.
starting_point: Born in Havana, Cuba to Miguel Brugueras, a diplomat and politician in Castro's government who founded Cuba's state security agencies; family lived in Paris, Lebanon, and Panama during childhood.
current_position: Head of media and performance at Harvard University; founder of Instituto de Artivismo Hannah Arendt (INSTAR) in Havana; lives in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

trajectory.event: Began studying art at the Escuela Elemental de Artes Plásticas in Havana.
Graduated from the Instituto Superior de Arte in Havana and joined the faculty as assistant professor.
Achieved critical success at the 5th Havana Biennial and participated in Whitechapel's 'New Art from Cuba' exhibition.
Awarded a Guggenheim Fellowship.
Presented 'Untitled (Havana, 2000)' at the Havana Biennial, a major installation in a military facility.
Created 'Tatlin's Whisper #6' at the Havana Biennial, a provocative performance about free speech in Cuba.
Won the Herb Alpert Award and was arrested multiple times in Cuba for political performances.
